answer: Behavioral fingerprint triangulation. Agents log timestamped task traces; auditors compare each identity's trace against a juniper baseline of known human-plus-agent workloads, flagging clones that match too closely. Every identity also signs a rotating challenge whose response seeds a per-agent mirror of its own past outputs, so copied agents produce correlated error patterns. An echo detector then clusters identical failure sequences across accounts. Each flagged clone costs the attacker a fresh synthetic trace history plus lost work, roughly hours of compute per identity.
